//: AWL Factions tuning defaults — canonical source of truth for all FactionTuning parameters.
//2: Edit tuning.json (Instance/Factions/) for live server overrides; this file ships with the plugin.
//3: New parameters belong here ONLY. They propagate to tuning.json on the next Flush.
//haulhull: A haul picks its hull by fuel credits per litre carried (HaulRankHullsByFuel; false = largest hold first). A convoy filling less than HaulMinLoadFraction of the hold is held unless its demand's urgency reaches HaulHoldUrgency; before holding, the first HaulSmallHullSearchNodes haul-stock nodes are searched for a hull the load fills to that fraction, fetched via a pickup leg. Urgency: catalogue 1.0 fresh and starved, recipe input 2.0, fuel 2.5, install 3.0, ship build 4.0, times starvation and (1 + age). FAC-393.
//gasprice: Gas is priced per KILOLITRE while gas inventory counts litres, because a credit per litre is not expressible in the integer a price is. SE's own MinimumHydrogenPrice/MinimumOxygenPrice are quoted per kilolitre and default to 300 each; the live catalogue takes them from the faction types, and these two are what answers when it cannot. ItemCredits is where a litre count meets one of these.
//FuelDepotOrderedIceCover: The ice cover the FuelDepot growth stage uses when the target region holds less ice than this share of one level-hour but an extraction order for ice is open: the order is ice on its way, so the request still posts. 0 turns the order path off and a depot region with no ice held waits (THROUGHPUT_HOLD FuelDepot reason=no-ice).
//MaxFarmUpgrades: Maximum Farm level. A level is one irrigation system and the 30 farm plots it waters.
//FarmIceScale: Ice a Farm burns per litre of water SE's farm plot draws. SE's literal figure is about 467 ice per fruit net of the replant seed; 0.025 makes a fruit cost about 12 ice, roughly half its price. Scales every crop alike, so SE's ratios between crops stand.
//MaxHabitatUpgrades: Maximum Habitat level. A level is the medical room, kitchen and beds it installs; its beds are the workers it houses.
//WorkerNutritionPerHour: Nutrition one worker eats per hour, in SE's Food stat units (1.00 = one MealPack_SteakDinner). SE's character food stat empties in 26.9 minutes: 2.23 an hour, unscaled.
//WorkerOxygenPerHour: Litres of oxygen one worker breathes per hour: SE's character OxygenConsumption of 0.063 a second, unscaled.
//WorkerUnfedLeavePerHour: Share of the workers a node cannot feed or give air to that leave per hour. Only the unfed share leaves.
//WorkerFoodReserveHours: Hours of food a Habitat asks to hold for its workers (Need: + Item: rows, class Upkeep) and keeps back from haulers.
//WorkerRecruitPrice: Credits one recruit costs at a node on a body with a civilian pool (Tellus).
// TransitCatchOdds: Read only while the fleet-trespass switch is on. The chance a carrier whose stay in hostile space outlasts the owner's shadow time is met by a Guard standing at the node. Scales the expected loss a route through hostile space is priced at (TransitRisk). A starting point: calibrate from TRESPASS_CATCH against TRANSIT_LEG counts.
// TransitDetourMaxStretch: The longest detour around hostile space a carrier considers, as a multiple of the route it replaces. A bound on the geometry; within it fuel against expected loss decides.
//munitions: MunitionDrawMode 1: every armed fleet draws a full load of magazines (what its weapons' inventories hold) from its departure node, fires only what it drew, and returns the rest to node stock where its hulls land; a prefab's own pre-loaded magazines are never credited. A combat fleet (Raid, Retaliate, Conquer, Guard, Patrol, Reinforce) the node cannot fully arm departs short and writes MUNITIONS_SHORT; a non-combat fleet draws only stock above what the node's parked combat hulls need. 0 turns it off: every fleet fires its bands without limit, as before. CombatTurnFireSeconds is the sustained fire one duel turn stands for, which sizes what a turn spends; first-pass value, not measured. A combat departure that flies short posts the missing magazines at its node as a Need: row, with an Item: row for the full load, both class Fuel, for MunitionShortfallDemandMinutes, so hauls move ammunition to where fleets leave from; 0 posts nothing. Every founded node also posts a standing reserve each production cycle of MunitionReserveLoads full loads for the combat hulls parked there (same Need:/Item: rows, class Fuel); 0 turns the standing reserve off. A load is sized by estimated use, not by the weapons' inventories: each weapon group's magazines per second x CombatTurnFireSeconds x the duel turns it is in range for x MunitionSortieDuels, never less than what its weapons hold (a Naginata: 222 artillery shells and 78 railgun slugs, against the 99 and 36 its turrets hold). On a materialised grid what the weapons cannot hold goes to cargo, as conveyor-fed stock. A materialised station draws the same sortie load for its own weapons from its node when it stands (the scan's or prefab's own magazines are stripped and credited nothing), is read and topped back up from node stock every StationMunitionTopUpSeconds (0 = load once at spawn), and hands back what is aboard when it despawns; what a read finds gone is booked as consumption. The standing reserve and the stock a non-combat fleet leaves alone both include one station load.
//patrolfuel: PatrolFuelRanking: a Patrol flies the hulls that cost least fuel for its whole circuit (origin, stops, home; valued at the origin as Haul values fuel) while meeting the circuit's threat - the strongest hostile raid inbound or holding at a circuit node now, or recorded attacking one within PatrolThreatMemoryHours. With no known threat it flies the posture-sized count, cheapest per DPS. Ion hulls that can lift cost ~0 and win. false restores strongest-first.
// PlayerOfferTtl: Seconds any offer (truce, non-aggression, alliance) stays open when either side is a player faction. Real time. NPC-to-NPC offers keep PeaceOfferTtl / PactOfferTtl. 0 turns the player window off.
// PactDefenceRelationBoost: Standing the owner of a defended node gains toward a pact partner whose Guard destroys a raid on that node. Paid only on an intercept, only to an ally, and never for a faction defending its own node. Equal to RaidRelationHit so one exercised pact offsets one raid -- an alliance that is used stays warm, which is what keeps a partner willing to spend hulls on it. 0 disables the lift.
// MemberReputationSyncEnabled: While a player is a member of a registered player faction, SE's personal reputation shows each managed NPC's standing toward that faction; the member's own record is kept in member_reputation.json and written back when they leave. false writes every record back and stops projecting.
// SeizeObjectiveQualityBoost: Quality bonus on a Raid or Conquer whose target sits in a region an active SeizeRegion campaign objective names -- what makes a colonisation beachhead push inward instead of settling. A weighting, not a filter: a faction pursuing an objective still answers a rival at its back. Larger than the grudge boost because a seize objective is a standing decision the faction paid a colonisation cost to make, where a grudge is a reaction.
// LaneConquestQualityBoost: Most quality a conquest gains for a region whose space costs this faction's lanes (risk accepted, detour fuel, escorts, robberies; decaying with a 12 h half-life). Half applies when the lanes have cost ConquerCost.
// RaidPredationAggressionFloor: Aggression at or below which a faction mounts no PREDATORY raid -- it still raids owners below HostileRelationThreshold (the whole pre-FAC-273 rule) but never picks a target it has no quarrel with. Above the floor predation ramps to 1.0 at maximum aggression and multiplies the candidate's want x weakness score. 0.5 separates raider (0.9) and factorum (0.9) from default (0.4), settler (0.3) and mercantile.
// RaidWarmTargetQualityPenalty: Score multiplier on a predatory raid whose owner the raider holds at a WARM standing, ramped by how warm: no penalty at 0, the full multiplier at or above AllyRelationThreshold. Same shape and value as TruceBreachQualityPenalty -- a raider with a fat enough target will occasionally bite the hand, and a merchant never gets this far because predation already zeroed its score.
//zone: relativeG (g / that planet's own true surface g) >= SurfaceGravityThreshold -> Surface; else any g>0 -> Orbit; g==0 -> DeepSpace. OrbitGravityMin is now the Orbit snap-band's RELATIVE ceiling (how tightly Orbit nodes get snapped), not a classification floor.
//twr: prefab must clear this dry (no-cargo) Down-thrust/weight ratio at both origin and destination gravity to be route-eligible; placeholder pending real scanned numbers (see docs/thrust-aware-prefab-selection-plan.md Open Questions)
//classFloors: minimum stats a prefab must clear to be classified Trade/Ferry/Gift, Raid/Patrol/Guard, or Mine -- not just nonzero. Cargo floors are first-pass placeholders sized to exceed a single incidental block's uncompensated bounding-box volume (15,625 L for one Large block, 125 L for one Small block -- see ScanPrefab's cargo fallback formula) without yet being observed against real prefab-mix data; Dps/drill floors start at 0 (nonzero-only) pending a live sample. All: live-tuning pass pending.
//fleetspeedtiers: A leg is flown at the cap of the ground under it, not at one speed end to end. Inside a body's gravity (natural g above FsdGravityDropoutG) the drive refuses, so the cap is FleetSpeedMinKmPerMin -- the world's own large-grid limit, derived at session load from LargeShipMaxSpeed. An authored NodeZone.Orbit region that is NOT in gravity (Cauldron's ring outboard of its 304.89 km gravity limit) is capped at FleetSpeedOrbitKmPerMin. Everything else is FleetSpeedKmPerMin. Gravity outranks the authored zone, which is the inverse of the placement rule: a ring cannot make the drive run where it refuses. A value of 0, or one outside [FleetSpeedMinKmPerMin, FleetSpeedKmPerMin], leaves an authored region flying as the open space around it.
//gridreap: A pass walks every grid in the world and judges MECHANICAL GROUPS, not grids: a rotor-mounted turret is its own grid, so grid-at-a-time judging would reap the turrets off a hull a fleet is still flying. A group is closed when some member carries the NPC-spawned bit or this process's mark, no fleet holds any member, it is not a station or a respawn grid, no UNMARKED member belongs to a non-NPC identity, and it is either older than the grace or has no player within ObservationRadiusKm + 1 km. Dry run: 'factions grids reap'; census: 'factions grids census'.
//fuel: FuelBurnScale multiplies every modelled burn and is set from the plan's verification ratios. ThrusterCruiseSpeedMs is the speed the ACCELERATING end of a thruster stretch is flown at (a launch, capped by the flight controller's handoff) and ThrusterApproachSpeedMs the BRAKING end (a descent, which nothing caps until braking starts); measured live at 100.1 and 420.1 m/s. Hover seconds are length/speed, apportioned half to each end on a stretch that does both, and each end costs its own speed in delta-v; the launch value is the flight controller's own LaunchHandoffSpeedMs and the two should agree. The Fsd* values are the RC.4 FSD Supercruise mod's own, read from the live FSDriveConfig.cfg: the drive refuses above FsdGravityDropoutG (absolute g), draws (Base + 1 + Multiplier*v/vmax + m*(1+v_kms^2)/0.528e6)/Divider MW in cruise and Base + FsdChargeMwPerKg*m for FsdChargeSeconds on entry. ReactorFuelKgPerMwh is SE's reactor FuelInfo (Mass 1, Ratio 1). FuelDrawMode is how far the model is wired in: 0 off (nothing priced, nothing recorded), 1 measure (every leg priced into the in-memory fuel ledger, read with 'factions fuel'; no inventory, credit, demand row or dispatch decision is touched), 2 draw (the default: each leg takes its burn from the departing node's stock).
//fuelreserve: FuelDrawMode 2 only. A departing hull takes its burn out of the node it leaves. With FuelImportPremium above 0 the shortfall is bought through the treasury at price x premium; at 0, the default, nothing is bought, the hull flies short, and the missing units are posted at the node as a Need: row (plus a gross Item: row) for FuelShortfallDemandMinutes. Every founded node also posts max(FuelBurnEma x FuelReserveHours, FuelReserveFloor) as a standing Need: row with an Item: row beside it; FuelBurnEma is that node's own burn per hour -- what departing legs needed, met or not -- decaying by e over FuelBurnEmaHours, and it also sizes FuelDepot upgrades. Parked hulls raise the row's urgency by FuelUrgencyPerParkedHull each, capped at FuelUrgencyHullCap. factions fuel reports short_share = short / (drawn + imported + short), per faction: the ramp-up number. MEASURED 2026-09-19 on v0.267.0: ~146 GL/day of hydrogen network-wide at 242 kL a leg, against 12 installed depot levels of the ~113 needed (1.296 GL/day each).
//fuelbuffer: FuelDrawMode 2 only. A departure node's buffer is its FuelBurnEma x FuelBufferLeadHours, capped at FuelBufferMaxFloors x the key's reserve floor; 0 at a node nothing departs from. It is a floor under the reserve above, and the catalogue gas top-up that shares the node's Item: row may not write that row below it while the node holds less. Lead MEASURED 2026-09-29 00:00-02:00 box-local: first FUEL_SHORT to next Gas:Hydrogen HAUL_RESOLVED at the node p50 6.5 min, p90 17.3, p95 22.9. FUEL_BUFFER (factions debug fuel) logs a node's buffer when it changes by a quarter or more.
//routecost: A leg's route is chosen by what it costs, not only by whether it collides. Candidates clear the body whose gravity well the direct line spends the most length inside, at each radius that body can be cleared at (low pass, orbit band, gravity limit), and the cheapest wins. Cost is minutes + RouteFuelWeightPerMinute x (the burn priced at FuelDraw import credits). 0 ranks on time alone and skips pricing candidates: time already carries most of the fuel saving, since hover is charged per second inside a well and is ~95% of this world's gas burn.
//planetroute: LowAltitudeKm is the low-pass floor above surface radius, offered only to hulls whose scanned thrust clears MinDryTwr down there; everything else arcs along the OrbitGravityMin shell that Orbit nodes snap to. ClearanceKm is the fallback shell for bodies with no usable gravity baseline.
//cruiseclamp: Cruise speed is granted per grid, not fixed: CruiseCapMs = sqrt(TerminalSpeed^2 + 2*a*budget) where budget = ObservationRadiusKm*1000/ApproachHorizonMargin - ApproachTerminalRadiusM. `a` is the braking authority the grid has actually been OBSERVED to deliver, held down to the thrust estimate -- a hull whose dampener under-delivers is granted less speed, not more. Until a grid has produced BrakeObservationMinSamples braking samples it is capped at ApproachCruiseSpeedMs, so nothing flies faster than today before it has demonstrated it can stop.
//launchclearance: The launch profile thrusts at the destination from the moment it engages, and a grid parked against a station is routinely on the wrong side of it -- a departure straight through the hull, with SE's own avoidance off because the grid is under native control. The probe picks the least-deflected departure bearing whose corridor is clear for LaunchClearanceM.
//flightavoid: Steer-around term in every native manoeuvre (approach and launch). Threat = closest approach of the two bounding spheres (+ FlightAvoidMarginM) within FlightAvoidLookaheadSec; the command is bent toward the sidestep in proportion to urgency. Obstacles are dynamic grids and characters only; static grids and voxels stay with the clearance probes.
//survey: SurveyTargetShare is the smallest fraction of a node's ground a survey must resolve before it stops. It must stay TIGHTER than a first sample, or the paced survey never runs: a planet catchment's first sample is 9,279 probes at 5 km and 20,878 at 7.5 km. 0.0008 asks for ~338,000, which is roughly the texel count of a 7.5km catchment - probing past that re-reads ground already read. SurveyDurationHours is how long a full survey takes, and it is a DURATION rather than a rate because the survey advances one node per frame: a fixed probes-per-tick means a different duration on every estate size, and the retired SurveyProbesPerTick=1 had drifted from the week it was set for to 50 days as the estate grew from 110 nodes to 760. The per-visit budget is derived from this and the live rotation size, capped by SurveyMaxProbesPerTick. SurveyDeclinesBeforeParking evicts a node the ore seam keeps refusing, so it stops consuming a share of the rotation forever (FAC-213).
// ResurveyMinimumPoints: Least ground a re-survey covers before it replaces a deposit measured in older units, however little the old one had looked at. The re-survey runs one node per frame at SurveyMaxProbesPerTick and keeps the old reading live until it is done. 20878 is a first sample over a 7.5 km catchment.
//resourceValue: A node's worth is derived, never rolled. A mineable node starts at UnsurveyedResourceValue and rises toward what its survey measures. Worth is value per unit of GROUND, not per unit of ore: the deposit's density (ore-band metres per probe) times what that ore is worth in multiples of the world's ordinary ore, read LOGARITHMICALLY against ResourceValueSaturationPerProbe. A node SAMPLED and found empty has nothing to survey and sits at its cap; a node the seam never answered for gets UnsurveyedResourceValue, because not looking is not the same as finding nothing (FAC-139). Every ore is priced AS ORE (Ore:<x>), never by its bare subtype, which reads the ingot (FAC-191). ResourceValueSaturationPerProbe is the top of the measured range: over the 789 sampled nodes of the live estate on 2026-10-09, ore-priced value-per-ground ran 0.72 / 16.2 / 138.5 (min / p50 / max) in one spread; 140 on a log curve lands it at p25 0.39 / p50 0.58 / p75 0.82. RareDepositValueRatio labels a deposit rare when its mix is worth that many times iron per unit of ore: SE ores run 1x to 3.5x, and 2.0 labelled 72 of those 789 nodes.
//abandonment: Losing a node forfeits 1 - SurveyRetainedOnAbandonment of its surveyed points. Composition and density come through unchanged - only the certainty behind them - so a reclaimed node still knows what its ores are and re-earns how sure it is. At a week-long full survey this costs days.
//richness: How MUCH ore is under a node, as against what the ground is WORTH. Every yield and drill-rate path scales by this; ResourceValue above is price-weighted and drives claim/found/raid scoring instead. The two are close to inversely ordered live, which is why they are two numbers: measured 2026-08-31 over the 654 well-surveyed nodes of the live estate, rare seams run ~8 ore-band metres per probe against iron's and ice's ~12, while the same nodes' ResourceValue spans 0.18 to 0.91 - all of that spread is ore price (FAC-219). RichnessSaturationMetresPerProbe is the world's ORE-ABUNDANCE knob and the one to turn to make the map richer or leaner: lower is more generous. Read LINEARLY, unlike ResourceValueSaturationPerProbe, because density spans one and a half decades (0.63 / 12.00 / 21.29 min / p50 / max) rather than four - a log curve would flatten exactly the 8-17 band holding 85% of the mass. 22 is MINT-NEUTRAL: richness summed over all 1039 live nodes totals 377.1 against the 374.4 those same nodes carry as ResourceValue today, so this redistributes ore between node types without changing how much the world mints. Nothing live reaches the cap. A node with no deposit reads 0 rather than the floor, or the floor would open a mint at every deposit-less node in the graph.
// FeatureMaxDensityPer1000Km3: The ceiling a world feature's 0..1 Density scales against, in objects per 1000 km3. A feature's Density is deliberately the same 0..1 shape as SE's own ProceduralDensity slider, so the absolute number lives here once rather than in every authored feature. 1350.0 is the live-tuned Cauldron value (2026-08-25): at Density 0.75 in a 3.6 km-thick ring it puts roughly 2,550 objects inside a 15 km view sphere -- a belt you fly through rather than scattered debris. Raising it makes every feature in the world denser without editing world_features.json.
// MaxFeatureRockSpawnsPerTick: Per-tick cap on newly spawned rock OBJECTS in the lazy view ring; the time-critical sync ring gets 4x this. Counted per object rather than per cell because at belt densities one cell is several synchronous AddVoxelMap calls, and an unbounded burst is the documented voxel-stall cause.
// FeatureRockGeneratorVersion: The SE asteroid generator VERSION handed to CreateAsteroidShape's 4th argument -- not an index into anything. Pinned here rather than read from the world's VoxelGeneratorVersion so a settings change cannot reshape rock regenerated later, and so a client rebuilding the same rock agrees. MUST be greater than 2: MyCompositeShapes returns early below that and never builds the material lists, which silently disables authored-ore control.
// FeatureRockCellSizeKm: Side in km of the cubic cell the rock grid spawns and despawns in units of. Determinism is per cell -- a cell's contents derive from (worldSeed, feature, cellCoord), so one can be torn down without touching another and nothing per-object is persisted. Sized against the world's ViewDistance: at 15 km a player's ball spans ~113 cells.
// FeatureRockShell: Rock shells (switch 'factions feature rock-shell', on at boot): the server spawns pristine feature rock only inside a shell around each player, phantom, and moving grid or character within FeatureRockShellAnchorRangeKm of one; linked clients are named the planned rock out to FeatureRockViewKm and build it themselves. At rest a shell is a sphere of SideKm; at or above MinSpeedMs it is an egg on the velocity: SideKm laterally, BackKm behind, SideKm + LeadSeconds x speed ahead. A rock spawns inside the shell shrunk by Hysteresis and closes outside the full shell. Side 3 km covers every server-side voxel query measured from the body that asks (autopilot avoidance <= 3 km, solar-shadow ray 3 km, mod turret targeting 2.8 km, AI Offensive / target lock 2.5 km). Placement probes (space respawn, fleet spawn) first spawn rock within PlacementRadiusM of the candidate, at most PlacementMaxSpawns, and hold it PlacementHoldSeconds. ViewKm 0 = SE's ViewDistance.
// FeatureRockSpawnBudgetMs: Per-frame time budget for spawning feature rock, ms. At least one rock is spawned per frame when any is queued; the rest wait. One AddVoxelMap is ~0.4 ms.
// StationDespawnGraceSeconds: A materialised station closes this long after no observer is within ObservationRadiusKm + 1 km, the radius fleet hulls despawn at. 0 = at once.
// StationQuiet: Switch 'factions feature station-quiet' (on at boot): a standing station with no player or phantom within StationQuietKm stops receiving entity updates; collision, damage and replication are untouched. It wakes inside StationQuietKm, or while a moving grid is within StationQuietWakeCombatKm, and quiets again past StationQuietKm + StationQuietHysteresisKm.
